subject: Daily AcreetionOS Update -- August 20, 2026
body:
Daily AcreetionOS Update - August 20, 2026

Dear AcreetionOS community,

We hope this newsletter finds you well. As we continue to work on our sovereign Linux distribution, we wanted to take a moment to highlight some of the recent developments and updates.

Firstly, we're excited to announce that we've been keeping up with the latest developments in the Go programming language. The recent release of Go 1.27 has been integrated into our codebase, ensuring that our distribution stays up-to-date with the latest advancements in the Go ecosystem.

In other news, our team has been busy working on various projects, including the AcreetionOS launcher, which now features a README with build badges and a feature overview. We've also made significant progress on our Xlibre build, adding the necessary dependencies and fixing conflicts.

On the infrastructure front, we've made some changes to our build systems, including the removal of unnecessary security and monitoring scripts to reduce failure points. This will help us to improve the stability and reliability of our builds.

We're also pleased to announce the initial commit of our Proxmox image, which will allow users to easily deploy AcreetionOS on their Proxmox servers. This is an exciting development, and we're looking forward to seeing how our community will utilize this feature.

In addition to these updates, our team has been working on various other projects, including the AcreetionOS wiki, which is now being updated regularly with new guides and tutorials. We're committed to providing our community with the resources they need to get the most out of our distribution.

As always, we're grateful for the support and contributions of our community. Your feedback and suggestions are invaluable to us, and we're always looking for ways to improve and expand our distribution.

If you're interested in getting involved with the AcreetionOS project, we encourage you to join our Discord server, where you can connect with other community members, ask questions, and share your ideas.

Finally, we want to thank you for being part of the AcreetionOS community. We're excited to see what the future holds for our distribution, and we're grateful to have you along for the ride.

Best regards,
Natalie Cole-Clift Spiva and Darren Clift
